kinds.practice: A ruling on something criminal where you are reading
kinds.hate: Passages capable of being read as incitement against a group

excerpt: This page carries only an excerpt.
The source publishes the opening and breaks off, with the remainder behind a separate document that has not been obtained. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends.
partial: This text breaks off before the Sheikh gives his own position.
It sets out the question, and in several cases the disagreement among scholars, but the source stops before he states his view. Do not read the last position stated here as his ruling — it is not.
cmsdate: The date shown is not the date of composition.
The source serves a bulk-upload timestamp; several texts are demonstrably years older than their stamp.
dated: It records what was said at the time, in the circumstances of that time. It is not a statement about the present, and nothing here has been updated.
context: This text has to be read whole.
Its parts depend on each other, and passages lifted out of it can be made to say close to the opposite of what is being argued. That is why the full text is here rather than a summary.
unsourced: A report here is given without a source.
The Sheikh names no collection, no chain and no grading, and none has been added. Its standing has not been established by this edition.
sensitive: This is a study text, not guidance to act on. It has been translated faithfully and has not yet been checked by a qualified reviewer, and the subject is one on which scholars and communities differ sharply.
polemic: Polemical terms have been carried into English.

The Arabic uses charged words for named communities. They have been rendered literally rather than neutralised, because softening them would misreport the source. They are the speaker’s words, not this edition’s.
